answer: A layered bond puts each identity on a mesa of three locked layers. The first costs 25 credits; each higher layer is a bridge that only verified work can cross, locked until all three clear. Auditors run each layer through a prism splitting shared funding apart: one funder behind many burns the stack. The k-th fake costs 25+8(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 4,021,000 vs a 40,000 pool; an honest agent pays 25 once. Rented layers fail the prism test.
